newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks inch up on mild bargain-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks inch up on mild bargain-hunting.

text.p: Mexican stocks notched up slight gains at the open on Tuesday on what dealers said was moderate bottom-fishing, after share prices had been hit the day before.

"That's the way it goes, the market hits prices and then it gets a second wind. There were a lot of small cross trades at flat prices at the open, but also light buying by local investors," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index was up 4.05 points in the opening minutes of trade, or 0.10 percent, at 4,130.35.
Trading volume was light at 2.7 million shares, but more active than early dealing on Monday.
Dealers said early gains on Wall Street had little impact on the bourse, which was reacting to local factors.
"There's no direct link. Telmex ADRs are flat but the L share here is up a couple of ticks; but that's a slight local rebound," a desk trader said.
The Dow Jones was meanwhile up 18.49 points to 7,496.99.
Telmex L shares was up four centavos to 18.66 pesos, while its ADRs were unchanged at 46-7/8.
Mexico's two biggest financial groups, Banacci and Bancomer, drove market gains on what most dealers said was a technical rebound.

Some dealers, however, noted the financials had traded more briskly than usual during recent sessions, and put demand down to speculation on a forthcoming plan to restructure mortgage debts held by banks.
Bancomer B shares were up six centavos to 3.43 pesos, while Banacci had gained 10 centavos to 18.90 pesos. The two stocks accounted for some 30 percent of shares traded in early dealing.
Dealers also drew attention to firm gains by corn flour and tortilla company Maseca, up 24 centavos to 7.84 pesos, following an announcement of a new government subsidy plan introduced on Monday.
Traders said profit-takers could soon step back into the market, as they did on Monday.
"I don't think it will gain much, there's no volume," one trader said.
On the broad market, of 37 stocks traded, gainers outnumbered sliders by 11 to nine.
